name: Doctor can review a synthetic patient and ask Mia for references
covers: ClinicalTrials.gov search link with Egypt location filter
WHO ICTRP and PubMed research discovery
Egyptian Drug Authority medication information and adverse-reaction links
trial records clearly separated from prescribing approval
description: Exercises the primary doctor journey from dashboard through a synthetic patient appointment to source-cited chat, without prescribing.
steps: Open the dashboard and verify the 'SYNTHETIC DATA ONLY' badge.
Open Appointments and select 'Antenatal follow-up' for Demo Patient A.
Open Mia chat, ask 'Find guidance for postpartum haemorrhage', and submit.
Review the returned links and the safety note.
Open Trials & info from the navigation.
Enter 'endometriosis' as the research topic and 'synthetic test intervention' as the optional intervention; keep Egypt selected.
Click Build source searches and verify links appear for ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, PubMed, NIH LactMed, DailyMed and the Egyptian Drug Authority.
Verify ClinicalTrials.gov search is Egypt-focused and the page requests research terms only, not patient case details.
Verify the EDA Drug Information Center contact details and the trial-versus-treatment boundary are visible.
expected: The appointment shows synthetic history; Mia displays relevant clickable source links and explicitly says no approved medication pathway is configured. No dental navigation appears. Trials & info builds public research queries and surfaces Egypt-specific medicine-information/safety sources without turning a registry record or search result into a medication recommendation; no patient data is submitted or stored.

name: Questionnaire supports conditional intake and local demo submission
description: Checks that questionnaire branching follows pregnancy status and submission is labelled as a browser demo.
steps: Open Questionnaires.
Change 'Are you currently pregnant?' to 'No' and verify the gestational-week field is hidden.
Change the answer back to 'Yes', complete the required fields if needed, and click 'Mark demo intake submitted'.
expected: The gestational-week field appears only when 'Yes' is selected. Submission shows the browser-demo confirmation and clinician-verification warning; no real patient link is issued.

name: Unknown allergies are never represented as a negative finding
description: Checks the mobile patient view preserves unknown allergy status and the safety warning.
steps: At mobile viewport, open Patients and select Demo Patient B.
Inspect the Allergies & reactions card.
Open Mia chat and review the visible synthetic-only boundary.
expected: The profile displays 'Unknown' and 'Must confirm', not 'No known allergies', and identifies the record as synthetic.

name: Jurisdiction filters do not present US-only guidance as Egypt authority
covers: US-only source exclusion in Egypt mode
description: Verifies a reference search in Egypt mode returns Egypt/global sources and excludes US-only ACOG guidance.
steps: Open Mia chat and set jurisdiction to 'Egypt · EG'.
Ask 'preeclampsia hypertension pregnancy' and send.
Review the source results and source jurisdiction labels.
expected: The results may show Egypt/global references but not ACOG's US-only practice bulletin. The interface labels the response source discovery and does not recommend a drug.

name: Arabic UI toggle, avatar customization, and governance warning are available
description: Checks localization controls, client-only avatar selection and the production readiness block.
steps: Click the Arabic language toggle and verify the main navigation changes to Arabic and layout direction switches.
Open the profile menu and select the Clinician avatar preset.
Open Safety & readiness.
expected: Arabic navigation and RTL layout appear; the local avatar changes without uploading a portrait; readiness states live clinical use is blocked and warns not to enter real patient data.
